# SEO-058: Build canonical URLs from configuration rather than the request Host header

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

The origin used in canonical values comes from deployment configuration or a validated host allowlist, never from the unvalidated Host or X-Forwarded-Host header of the incoming request.

## Rationale

A canonical assembled from an attacker-supplied header lets any host that reaches the application inject its own address into the page's canonical declaration, which turns a header injection into a canonicalization change on real pages.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Read the origin from an environment variable or config module at startup. If the deployment genuinely serves several hosts, validate the incoming host against an explicit allowlist and fall back to the primary origin when it does not match.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Send a request carrying a Host header for an unrelated domain and confirm the emitted canonical still names the configured origin.
- Evidence: `HTTP_HEADER`, `RENDERED_HTML`, `FILE`
- Automated check: none.

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
